intent: I have a total budget 120 dollars for my first mechanical keyboard, used for all-day office writing and shooters at night. I require a minimum switch experiment reserve 30 dollars, more than 61 physical keys, and noticeable feedback without Blue click; wired mode acceptable. Compare the RK100 Brown reserve, RK100 Red reserve, and Keychron K12 Red compact routes. Put reserve and layout before gaming marketing. Audit each frozen listing's price, remaining budget, key count, switch and hot-swap wording, connection path, review display, and profile or ergonomic claims. Explain what Red, Brown, linear, and tactile classifications do and do not establish, reconcile the conflicting owner preferences, and separate other model regrets from current model proof when discussing height discomfort or PCB failure. Recommend one route, keep seller claims and absent same-model validation explicit, and cite each factual claim to its sandbox source.

generator_view.scenario: A buyer has a total budget of $120 for a first mechanical keyboard used for all-day office writing and shooters at night. They need more than 61 physical keys, want at least $30 left for later switch experimentation, accept wired operation, want noticeable feedback, and want to avoid a Blue-style click in the office.
generator_view.target: Audit the frozen product claims, switch classifications, and conflicting owner reports, then choose one starting route without treating seller adjectives or other-model anecdotes as current-model performance, comfort, or durability proof.
